evals.expected_output: The draft-ui-redesign workflow runs first and writes docs/redesign/<page>-redesign.md; its section 3 prompt then becomes a Claude Design artifact created from a freshly quickstarted Design type, with separate artboards for every state and breakpoint, existing labels verbatim, the artifact URL written back into the doc, and the five-part hand-back report.
assertions: Runs the draft-ui-redesign workflow first (invoking that skill) and writes a redesign document under docs/redesign/ containing a section 3 generation prompt, before any Claude Design artifact is created
Creates the design by calling the Artifact tool with action quickstart and intent design, then publishing with the type_url that quickstart returned, rather than a hardcoded or remembered type link
Does not call DesignSync and does not hand off to, or write a prompt for, Stitch, v0, Lovable, or Figma Make
The design includes every currently rendered data point and control: available balance, the Request payout button, arrival date, amount, destination bank name with last 4 digits, and status
Designs loading, empty, error, and dense or overflowing states as separate artboards, plus at least one mobile-width artboard, not only the populated desktop view
Keeps the existing labels verbatim (Payouts, Request payout, Arrival date, Amount, Destination, Status) and adds no hero or marketing section above the balance and table
Writes the artifact URL into the top of the redesign document as a line of the form 'Claude Design: <url>'
Ends with a hand-back report listing the design link, the document path, the proposed API additions or 'none needed', whether frontend-design was used, and anything the user should review

evals.expected_output: The skill locates the page and its useMembers data source, sees there is no response shape to work from, and stops to ask for the hook, the handler, or a sample payload instead of creating a design. It does not create a Claude Design artifact and does not invent fields.
assertions: Does not create a Claude Design artifact: no Artifact quickstart with intent design and no publish with a Design type_url
Asks the user for the response shape, specifically the useMembers hook, the API handler behind it, or a sample payload
Explains that designing on guessed fields would produce a polished but wrong redesign, rather than complying with 'just go for it'
Identifies useMembers from @/lib/hooks/use-members as the page's data source
Does not invent member fields beyond those visible in the component (id, name, email, role), such as avatar, status, last active, or join date
Keeps any partial audit to what the component shows: the Team heading, the Invite member button, and the name, email, and role of each member

evals.expected_output: frontend-design (when installed) shapes the build through a token plan reviewed against the brief, but ranks below the redesign contract: the design opens on the issue table, keeps every existing label and action, adds no new features, and spends the user's 'bold' request on one detail inside a dense layout.
assertions: When Anthropic's frontend-design skill is available, invokes it before filling the Claude Design artifact, and does not substitute a community skill such as frontend-design-direction in its place

Records a compact design plan before building (a palette of 4 to 6 named hex values, typefaces with their roles, and a layout concept) and reviews it against the brief for generic defaults before building
The first artboard opens on the issue list itself, with no hero headline, marketing copy, or landing-page composition
Keeps the existing labels verbatim: Issues, Filter by assignee, Anyone, Me, Mark as done, Unassigned, and the Key, Title, Priority, and Assignee column headings
Adds no features, filters, or actions that the current page lacks, such as kanban drag-and-drop, bulk actions, search, or new filter options

Confines the bold treatment to one deliberate detail, such as the priority or state treatment or the issue key, while the overall layout stays dense and scannable, consistent with a named work-tracking benchmark mechanic
Preserves row-click navigation to /issues/:key and shows the Mark as done action only for issues that are not done
The hand-back report states whether frontend-design was used
